validity.researcher_notes: Existence: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM. Two San Diego Union-Tribune articles (Nikolewski, 2020-02-06 and 2020-03-18) describe Line 1600 in detail as SDG&E's existing 16-inch, ~50-mile natural gas transmission pipeline running from Rainbow Station (Fallbrook area) to Mission Station/Mission Valley, built 1949, serving ~150,000 eastern San Diego County customers. A federal PHMSA interpretation letter dated 2020-08-13 (addressed to SoCalGas, re: Line 1600 longitudinal joint factor) independently states 'Line 1600, a 50-mile San Diego Gas & Electric gas transmission pipeline located in San Diego County, California' originally constructed in 1949 with 16-inch A.O. Smith pipe -- a federal regulator source wholly separate from SDG&E's own filings and from the newspaper. A CPUC A.15-09-013 docket document (SDG&E/SoCalGas response to CPUC Data Request 7, 2018-03-06) gives 'Line 1600 (49.7 miles)' and 16-inch diameter pipe, and confirms it remains an active transmission pipeline (a competing 2015-2018 proposal to de-rate 45 miles of it to distribution service was DENIED by CPUC in 2018; the 2020 project that is actually proceeding, per the SDUT articles, replaces/hydrotests segments while KEEPING transmission service -- so PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas both hold). Classification: correctly a gas transmission pipeline, not gathering/distribution -- confirmed by PHMSA present-tense in 2020 ('Line 1600...gas transmission pipeline') and by the CPUC NOP document rejecting the de-rate-to-distribution alternative. Duplicate check against the 46-row roster: no other row plausibly describes this physical line -- P0207 Kern River and P0219 Mojave (the other two rows in the 'California import trio' the brief calls out) are both interstate FERC pipelines terminating near Bakersfield under an old El Paso lineage; Line 1600 is an intrastate SDG&E line entirely within San Diego County with no interconnect or corporate link to either. No duplicate. Attribution: Owner1='Sempra Energy [100%]' matches the SDUT articles' description of SDG&E as 'fellow Sempra Energy affiliate' (Sempra is SDG&E's parent holding company, confirmed independently on Wikipedia's SDG&E article) -- this is the correct ultimate-parent convention used elsewhere in this batch (cf. Kern River/Berkshire Hathaway in batch 3), so Owner1 is CONFIRMED, not a defect. Operator was blank and is filled below. Opened/read to exhaustion: both SDUT articles, the CPUC NOP, the CPUC DR7 responses, the CPUC SCGC-23 (DR23) responses, and the PHMSA interpretation letter -- 5 of the row's harvested/found documents opened, 2 more harvested citations (sdgenews.com, newsdata.com) attempted and one failed url_verifier (sdgenews.com 404) and one lacked the pipeline name (newsdata.com, only discusses the $677M cost generically).

validity.recommendation: correct Capacity from 630 MMcf/d to approximately 65 MMcf/d (Line 1600's own nominal capacity); 630 MMcf/d is SDG&E's total system capacity, not this segment's
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity=630.00 MMcf/d for Line 1600 itself does not survive source-checking -- it is SDG&E's SYSTEM-WIDE transmission capacity 'with Line 1600 operating at 640 psig', not Line 1600's own throughput. Two CPUC A.15-09-013 docket documents (SDG&E/SoCalGas's own regulatory filings, same overall proceeding but two separate data-request responses filed a year apart) state this explicitly: the 2018-03-06 DR7 response says 'The nominal capacity of Line 1600 as currently operating as part of the SDG&E transmission system is 65 MMcfd' (contrasted with proposed Line 3602 at 500 MMcfd); the 2017-09-19 SCGC-23 (DR23) response repeatedly frames 'system capacity with Line 1600 operating at 640 psig is 630 MMcfd' as the SDG&E SYSTEM total, and separately reports ACTUAL measured 2017 flows through Rainbow Metering Station into Line 1600 of only 29.96 MMcfd average / 46.32 MMcfd maximum -- an order of magnitude below 630 and consistent with the ~65 MMcfd nominal figure. This is independently corroborated by the wiki's own cited SDUT article, which says the line 'provides only about 10 percent of capacity for the San Diego area' -- 10% of the system's 630 MMcfd is ~63, matching the 65 MMcfd nominal figure almost exactly and confirming 630 was never meant to describe this segment alone. GEM's wiki page appears to have pulled '630 million cubic feet per day' from a generic EIA natural gas data portal (www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php) that url_verifier confirms does NOT name Line 1600 or state 630 anywhere -- a classic aggregate-figure-on-a-segment error, likely compounded by conflating the SDG&E-system figure with the segment figure. Recommend Capacity -> 65 (MMcf/d), sourced to the CPUC DR7 response; note the DR7/SCGC-23 pairing is one origin (both are SDG&E/SoCalGas's own regulatory filings in one docket), but the SDUT journalism (independent of the applicant) corroborates the ~10%-of-system proportion independently, and the actual 2017 flow data (29.96-46.32 MMcfd) is real-world telemetry that independently brackets the 65 MMcfd nominal figure from below. This is not a MISSING_VALUE fill -- the cell already carries a value, so it is staged here as a validity concern rather than a REFS_ADDED fill (the source does not agree with the sheet's 630); see the matching fills[] entry on Capacity, which is closed UNRESOLVED for the same reason and points back here.
